title: Where Your Flush Goes in 20 Seconds #shorts
summary: Test Short for the sewer world (not queued): follow one flush from the toilet through the lateral and the sewer main, up a lift station, through the treatment plant and out to the river.
sources: Over 800,000 miles of public sewers, plus about 500,000 miles of private lateral sewers that connect homes and businesses to public sewer lines (ASCE 2021 Report Card for America's Infrastructure, Wastewater, p.153): https://infrastructurereportcard.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Wastewater-2021.pdf

scenes.narration: You flush. It's gone. But where?
Down the lateral under your yard, and into the sewer main.
Over {800,000|eight hundred thousand} miles of public sewer. Where the ground rises, a pump lifts it.
A treatment plant cleans it. Then the water goes back to the river.
